proposal.actor: United States military and political decision authorities
proposal.action: Allow the standing order to continue and execute the second city attack as soon as operationally ready.
proposal.purpose: accelerate Japanese surrender and avoid continued and invasion casualties
proposal.requested_authority: Allow the standing order to continue and execute the second city attack as soon as operationally ready.

evidence.claim: An earlier directive authorised the first attack on specified targets and stated that additional weapons would be delivered against listed targets as soon as made ready.
The first weapon has now been used against an inhabited city and senior officials have reports showing destruction on an extraordinary city-wide scale.
Senior leadership has explicitly discussed the grave responsibility created by the weapon's demonstrated effects.
A major new allied belligerent has entered the war against the opponent, adding a new military front and materially changing the opponent's strategic position.
The opponent has not announced surrender by the time the second mission is being prepared.
The second weapon is operationally ready and can be used quickly under the existing directive unless senior authority intervenes.

It is uncertain how rapidly the first attack and the new belligerent's entry will affect the opponent's surrender decision; both events are new and their combined effect has had little time to develop.
Continuing the war also causes severe and accumulating harm through other military operations and preparation for invasion, so delay is not cost-free.
A second attack on an inhabited military-industrial city foreseeably risks very large civilian casualties similar in kind to the first use, though the precise number is unknown.
The standing repeated-use order was approved before either the first weapon's actual effects or the new belligerent's entry were known.

affected_parties.party: Civilians in the next target city
affected_parties.interests_or_risks: Foreseeable mass death, injury and destruction without individual participation in the targeting decision.

affected_parties.party: Military personnel and military-industrial facilities in the target area
affected_parties.interests_or_risks: Direct attack because of contribution to the continuing war.

affected_parties.party: Friendly military personnel and civilians exposed if the war continues
affected_parties.interests_or_risks: Death and injury from continued combat, conventional attack, blockade and possible invasion.
Pressure to surrender under newly worsened strategic conditions.
Ending the war rapidly, protecting friendly forces, maintaining operational momentum and accepting responsibility for repeated use of a novel mass-destruction weapon.
Precedent for repeated use, command/control norms and whether changed facts trigger fresh authorisation.

alternatives.description: Temporarily pause further uses and require explicit senior reassessment of necessity in light of the first attack, the new belligerent and any emerging response.
Issue a renewed surrender warning referring to the demonstrated destructive capability and changed strategic situation, then reassess after a defined short interval.
Require fresh top-level approval before every additional use rather than treating the earlier directive as continuing authority.
Continue other military operations during a short reassessment period instead of executing the second use immediately.
Pause only long enough for explicit senior review while other military pressure continues.
Require fresh authorisation for each further use after reassessing current evidence and alternatives.
Issue a renewed surrender demand/warning incorporating the first attack's demonstrated effect and the changed strategic position.
Continue with the second attack immediately under existing authority.
Defer further use while monitoring the opponent's response to the major shocks already delivered.

uncertainties: Whether the first use plus the new belligerent's entry will induce surrender without another attack and how quickly.
Whether a short pause materially increases friendly casualties or merely delays surrender.
Whether a renewed warning or changed terms would accelerate capitulation.
The precise civilian and military casualties from the next attack.
Whether opponent hard-liners can withstand further delay without surrender.
The long-term strategic effect of repeated use under standing authority.
requested_capability: Allow the standing order to continue and execute the second city attack as soon as operationally ready.
